From Wiktionary, the free dictionary

Latin

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

From Proto-Indo-European *peh₂w- (“to strike, hit”) (traditionally reconstructed as *paw-), and cognate with Lithuanian pjáuti (“to cut, reap”), Latvian pļaũt (“to mow, reap”), Ancient Greek παίω (paíō, “to strike, hit”).[1] See also paveō, pudeō, repudium, and tripudium.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • (Classical Latin) IPA(key): [ˈpa.wi.oː]
  • (modern Italianate Ecclesiastical) IPA(key): [ˈpaː.vi.o]

Verb

[edit]

paviō (present infinitive pavīre, perfect active pavīvī, supine pavītum); fourth conjugation

  1. to beat, strike
  2. to ram
  3. to tread down

Old Galician-Portuguese

[edit]

Alternative forms

[edit]
  • pavyo

Etymology

[edit]

    Inherited from Vulgar Latin *papīlum, from Latin papȳrus, borrowed from Ancient Greek πάπυρος (pápuros).[1] Doublet of papel and papiro.

    Pronunciation

    [edit]
    • IPA(key): /paˈβio/

    Noun

    [edit]

    pavio m (plural pavios)

    1. candlewick
      • 13th century, João Fernandes de Ardeleiro, O que ſeja no pauyo; republished as Angelo Colocci, compiler, Cancioneiro da Biblioteca Nacional, Italy, c. 1525–1526, cantiga 1327:
        O que ſeja no pauyo / Que me fez perder pauya / De que meu nada nom fio / Al mer fez comſa perfia: / De noyte per muy g̃m fryo / Que tangeſe en pella frya / Mays aynda mendeu ryo / Como sendel nũca ria.
        (please add an English translation of this quotation)

    Derived terms

    [edit]
    • seer no pavio

    Descendants

    [edit]
    • Galician: pabío
    • Portuguese: pavio

    References

    [edit]
    1. ^ Machado, José Pedro (1995), “Pavio¹”, in Dicionário etimológico da língua portuguesa [Etymological dictionary of the Portuguese language] (in Portuguese), 7 edition, volume IV (M–P), Lisboa: Livros Horizonte, →ISBN, page 325, column 2
    • Barreiro, Xavier Varela; Guinovart, Xavier Gómez (2006–2018), “pavio”, in Corpus Xelmírez: corpus lingüístico da Galicia medieval [Corpus Xelmírez: linguistic corpus of Medieval Galicia] (in Galician), Santiago de Compostela: Instituto da Lingua Galega
    • Cunha, Antônio Geraldo da (2020–2026), “pavio”, in Vocabulário histórico-cronológico do português medieval [Historical and chronological vocabulary of Medieval Portuguese] (in Portuguese), Rio de Janeiro: Fundação Casa de Rui Barbosa
    • Ferreiro, Manuel (2014–2026), “pavio”, in Universo Cantigas: edición crítica da poesía medieval galego-portuguesa [Universo Cantigas: critical edition of Galician-Portuguese medieval poetry] (in Galician), A Coruña: University of A Coruña, →ISSN
    • Seoane, Ernesto Xosé González; Granja, María Álvarez de la; Agrelo, Ana Isabel Boullón (2006–2022), “pavio”, in Dicionario de Dicionarios do galego medieval [Dictionary of dictionaries of Medieval Galician] (in Galician), Santiago de Compostela: Instituto da Lingua Galega

    Portuguese

    [edit]

    Etymology

    [edit]

    From Old Galician-Portuguese pavio, from Vulgar Latin *papīlum, from Latin papȳrus. Doublet of papiro.

    Pronunciation

    [edit]
    • (Brazil) IPA(key): /paˈvi.u/, /paˈviw/ [paˈviʊ̯]
     
    • (Portugal) IPA(key): /pɐˈvi.u/
    • (Portugal) IPA(key): /pɐˈvi.u/
      • (Northern Portugal) IPA(key): /pɐˈbi.u/ [pɐˈβi.u]

    • Rhymes: -iu
    • Hyphenation: pa‧vi‧o

    Noun

    [edit]

    pavio m (plural pavios)

    1. fuse (cord used to ignite a charge)
    2. wick (burning cord of a candle)
      Synonym: mecha

    Derived terms

    [edit]
    • de fio a pavio
    • pavio curto

    References

    [edit]
    • “pavio”, in Dicionário Aulete Digital (in Portuguese), Rio de Janeiro: Lexikon Editora Digital, 2008–2026
    • “pavio”, in Michaelis Dicionário Brasileiro da Língua Portuguesa (in Portuguese), São Paulo: Editora Melhoramentos, 2015–2026, →ISBN
    • “pavio”, in Dicionário infopédia da Lingua Portuguesa (in Portuguese), Porto: Porto Editora, 2003–2026
    • “pavio”, in Dicionário Priberam da Língua Portuguesa (in Portuguese), Lisbon: Priberam, 2008–2026
